_comment: Popularity inputs for tools/report_market.py. These are NOT measured by this repo. They are third-party survey figures, recorded here so the derived share estimate is auditable and reproducible. Update the figures and the retrieved date together.

so2025.name: Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025, 'Programming, scripting and markup languages', all respondents
so2025.measures: percentage of respondents who did extensive development work in the language over the past year; multi-select, so the column sums to far more than 100

octoverse2025.name: GitHub Octoverse 2025
octoverse2025.measures: monthly contributors per language on GitHub; TypeScript passed Python and JavaScript in August 2025

tiobe2026.name: TIOBE Index, August 2026
tiobe2026.measures: search-engine volume proxy, not developer count

_share_note: share = so2025 normalised across the languages in this file only, then widened by 15 percent either side. The band is deliberate: the sources disagree, and a single number would imply a precision nobody has.

javascript.note: Node.js leads web frameworks at 49.1 percent in the same survey

python.note: figure includes heavy data-science and AI use, not only backend

typescript.note: number one on GitHub by monthly contributors since August 2025

java.note: backend share is higher than the raw figure suggests; little front-end use

cpp.note: mostly systems, embedded and games; rarely an HTTP service

c.note: mostly systems and embedded; rarely an HTTP service

php.note: almost entirely backend, so its backend share exceeds the raw figure

go.note: top five in US job postings for cloud, API and infrastructure work

rust.note: entered the TIOBE top ten in July 2026; much use is systems, not backend

kotlin.note: split between Android and JVM backend work

ruby.note: almost entirely backend, via Rails; slowly declining

lisp.note: the survey category aggregates Common Lisp, Scheme and Emacs Lisp
